scenes.heading: What is Databricks?
scenes.narration: Databricks is a unified analytics platform built on Apache Spark that brings data engineering, data science, and analytics together in one place.

scenes.heading: What it unifies
scenes.narration: Databricks lets engineers build ETL pipelines on the same platform where analysts run SQL. It offers collaborative notebooks so teams share code and results in one workspace. And it hosts machine learning and dashboards, avoiding the cost of stitching separate tools together.

scenes.heading: From raw data to insight
scenes.narration: Data flows in from cloud storage and streaming sources into Databricks. Spark clusters ingest and transform it, writing reliable Delta Lake tables. Those curated tables then power dashboards and machine learning models for the whole organization.

scenes.heading: Lakehouse vs. two silos
scenes.narration: Traditionally teams kept a data lake for raw files and a separate warehouse for analytics, duplicating data and creating sync problems. The lakehouse keeps a single copy of data with warehouse-grade reliability. That means unified governance and consistently fresh tables.

scenes.text: Databricks is one platform for the whole data lifecycle, so engineering, analytics, and machine learning all work on the same trusted data.
scenes.narration: The core takeaway is that Databricks unifies the entire data lifecycle, letting every team work on the same trusted data.
